Propose foreign key relationships from the column profile

Source: R/foreign_keys.R
infer_foreign_keys.Rd

Tier-one inference, from profile statistics alone and without extra queries. Every column of a string, integer or uuid type is scored against every pk_candidate column in another table (or another column of the same table), and the best-scoring target above min_confidence is recorded. Confirming a candidate with a value match-rate query is the key register's job, later; this is the shortlist for it.

Usage

infer_foreign_keys(profile, min_confidence = 0.5)

Arguments

profile

A column_profile from db_profile(), ideally covering every table of interest: a key in a table that is not in profile cannot be proposed.

min_confidence

Lowest score that counts as a candidate.

Value

profile with fk_candidate (logical), fk_target (schema.table.column of the best key, or NA), fk_confidence, fk_evidence (the scoring components as text) and fk_n_targets (how many keys scored at or above min_confidence; a conformed code such as a site code legitimately matches several) added or replaced.

Details

A pair is ruled out when the types differ, the child's string lengths fall outside the key's, or the two columns share a value_fingerprint (a copy, not a reference). Surviving pairs score:

  • name evidence: 0.5 for the same normalised name, 0.35 when the child name ends with the key name (prior_mrn to mrn), 0.2 when it contains the key's table stem (ward_name to wards.ward_id);

  • range: 0.25 when both ranges are known and the child's min and max lie inside the key's, -0.25 when they do not; nothing when either side's values are suppressed or the key table was sampled;

  • cardinality: 0.15 for a many-to-one shape (the child has no more distinct values than the key and is not itself unique), 0.05 for one-to-one; skipped when either table was sampled;

  • 0.1 for passing the type and length checks at all.

Scores are capped at 1. Ties go to the key with more distinct values.

Examples

con <- fakehosp_connection()
inv <- db_inventory(con, include = c("pas_patients$", "pas_adt_events$"), progress = FALSE)
#> ℹ 2 tables found (sqlite dialect)
#> ✔ Inventory of 2 tables and 30 columns in 0s
prof <- db_profile(con, inv, progress = FALSE)
prof[prof$fk_candidate, c("table_name", "column_name", "fk_target", "fk_confidence")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   table_name     column_name fk_target             fk_confidence
#>   <chr>          <chr>       <chr>                         <dbl>
#> 1 pas_adt_events mrn         main.pas_patients.mrn          0.75
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
